text:
ana: pager triggered — billing metering heartbeat anomaly in eu1. token counts reported ~7% lower than expected starting 02:10 UTC. customers receiving overage badges. anyone oncall?
incbot: INCIDENT ALERT (P2) — billing-metering-heartbeat: token-drift detected in eu1. @oncall paged.
ryan: i'm on it, joining #incidents-call. can someone paste a quick sample of the discrepancy?
ana: (typo) ana: quick sample from aggregator at 02:12:
```
expected_tokens: 1,024,512
reported_tokens: 952,340
delta: -7.01%
heartbeat_ts_collector: 2025-06-12T02:12:08.231Z
heartbeat_ts_emitter: 2025-06-12T02:12:00.105Z
```
ryan: weird — emitter timestamps are ~8s behind collector. kafka consumer lag = 0, so messages are arriving but timestamped old. could be host clock drift or wrong NTP config.
sophie: checking deploys — no metering service deploys in the last 24h. infra changes?
jess: infra configs show NTP on host gke-node-77 had ntpd stuck, last sync 03:40 local. that would explain emitter timestamp retard.
ops-pager: annotating incident: probable root cause = host clock offset on emitter partition leader. potential customer impact = false low counts -> overage flags.
ana: practical mitigation: 1) suppress automatic overage notifications to affected customer cohort 2) enable fallback-shadow-counts until reconciliation 3) rotate leader to healthy host and restart ntp on affected nodes.
ryan: suppressing alerts now — runbook cmd: `POST /internal/billing/alerts/suppress?reason=heartbeat-timewarp&ttl=2h` — done :white_check_mark:
sophie: restarting ntp on hosts in eu1 affected pool: gke-node-75/76/77 — rolling restart kicked.
jess: scheduling backfill: once node clocks stable, we'll replay emitter logs and run reconciliation job. backfill ETA ~1.5h.
ana: customer impact note for comms: small subset (~12 customers, high throughput) saw temporary overage badges. no charges will be applied until reconciliation completes. ops to confirm.
ryan: adding eng-infra to thread and creating follow-up ticket: INFRA-6592 (ntp drift causing emitter timestamps)
incbot: oncall handoff recorded: @ryan -> primary. escalation added to eng-infra.
ops-pager: cross-check: are there any writes lost? kafka acks = all, so no data loss expected. only timestamp skew.
sophie: monitoring: I've put a short-term smoothing rule in the counting pipeline to ignore heartbeats older than 5s and to prefer collector timestamps when delta > 3s. live smoothing applied.
jess: started reconciliation job in dry-run mode — sample mapping shows corrected totals will remove overage badges for 9/12 customers. full run queued.
ana: I will draft the customer note: "We detected transient timestamp skew causing incorrect usage badges. We suppressed notifications and will reconcile usage — no customer charges expected. Updates in ~2h."
ryan: timeline: 02:10 anomaly started; 02:14 suppression + smoothing; 02:20 node restarts + ntp restart; 02:40 clocks stable; 03:00 reconciliation queued; expected closure after backfill at ~03:30.
incbot: UPDATE — incident state: mitigation in place, customer suppression active, reconciliation queued.
ana: any objections to moving to monitoring-only and close pager?
sophie: agree. continue to watch wildcards for 30m.
ryan: closing pager, keeping incident open for reconciliation verification. will post final summary after backfill.
incbot: INCIDENT NOTE: pager closed at 1772468370 by ryan.
ana: final — reconciliation completed at 1772468520, corrections applied; overage badges removed; no customer charges. marking incident resolved and creating postmortem draft.
incbot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — billing-metering-heartbeat-timewarp at 1772468520.
